matched_examples.anchor_excerpt: The notion that illnesses were constantly changing started to emerge in the late eleventh century when a few physicians applied to other disorders models that had been designed to understand Cold Injury. A prototypical case of Cold Injury unfolded in distinct stages that each called for a different treatment. Xu Shuwei's 許叔微 (1079-1154) Ninety Discussions on Cold Injury (Shanghan jiushi lun 傷寒九十論), written at the turn in the twelfth century but only printed for the first time in the nineteenth century, were early accounts of successful treatments based on unique diagnoses. $ ^{2} $
